rationale: The audience — software engineers and indie devs who follow tech news professionally — does demonstrably pay for curated newsletters (TLDR, The Pragmatic Engineer), confirming willingness_to_pay at a moderate level. However, buyer_clarity lands at 6 rather than higher because this is a prosumer/individual-consumer mix with real 'should be free' sentiment, and there is no named business role with a budget line. The build_gate for buyer_clarity (floor: 6) is met but barely, and responsiveness_signal is untested, so validate is the right stage before committing to build.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a weekly or twice-weekly curated email digest of non-AI tech news, filtered and summarised by Claude from RSS/HN/lobste.rs feeds. BUILD: the factory sets up a Claude prompt pipeline that ingests feeds, filters out AI-tagged stories, summarises the remainder into a scannable digest, and sends via a transactional email provider (e.g. Resend or Buttondown); a simple landing page with a Stripe subscription link ($8–12/mo) and an email sign-up form is the entire storefront — no coding by Youval. SELL: reach 300–500 potential subscribers by posting in HN threads (like the source thread), relevant subreddits (r/programming, r/webdev), and targeted cold emails to indie-dev communities; outreach copy is drafted by the factory and goes out only after Youval approves each batch. MAINTAIN: Claude runs the digest pipeline on a schedule, handles subscription confirmation/cancellation via Stripe webhooks, and auto-replies to support emails; Youval's only recurring touch is approving the weekly send and any refund requests. VALIDATE FIRST: before building, post a one-paragraph pitch in the HN thread and a waitlist form — if 50+ people sign up in 72 hours, proceed to build.
notes: buyer_clarity floor (6) is met at exactly the minimum. Defensibility is low — a determined competitor can replicate the filter. Validate with a waitlist before investing in the pipeline build.
